section_summary: This section records Allied occupation decisions on Japanese industrial reparations, including custody of shipyards and precision bearing plants and removal of synthetic oil, synthetic rubber, and steel rolling capacity. It also contains State Department and War Department correspondence about minimum industrial levels, the proposed Reparations Conference, and SCAP’s role. The final pages begin a London despatch enclosing a British parliamentary statement on Japan’s future industries and export trade.

subfiles.title: Information on reparations selections within the shipbuilding industry
subfiles.about: Instructions explain custody, maintenance, continued production, and possible removal of selected shipyard facilities.
subfiles.summary: SCAP directs preservation and periodic inspection of shipyard equipment selected for interim reparations while allowing production needed by occupation forces and civilians.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1136: Reparations selections within the precision bearing industry
subfiles.about: SCAP places listed precision bearing plants under its custody and control for possible reparations removal.
subfiles.summary: The directive allows operations to continue temporarily but subjects plants to removal after 30 days without further notice. Its enclosure lists 32 bearing plants and addresses across Japan.

subfiles.title: Information on SCAPIN 1136
subfiles.about: Implementation guidance describes maintenance, inspection, and permitted operation of selected bearing plants.
subfiles.summary: Guidance preserves bearing capacity worth 32.5 million yen while safeguarding surplus plants for removal.

subfiles.title: Removal of synthetic oil and synthetic rubber industries from Japan
subfiles.about: SWNCC forwards its approved policy paper and requests transmission to the U.S. member of the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Forwards approved SWNCC 315 and requests its delivery to the U.S. FEC representative.

subfiles.title: Transmission of SWNCC synthetic industries policy
subfiles.about: The U.S. representative is asked to present the synthetic oil and rubber removal policy to the Commission.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the approved U.S. policy and requests FEC consideration.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Commission decision on synthetic industries
subfiles.about: The FEC transmits its unanimous decision and requests a directive to SCAP and coordinated press release.
subfiles.summary: Johnson reports unanimous approval on 12 September and asks that a directive be sent to SCAP. Press release is to follow receipt in Tokyo by 48 hours, with security maintained during transmission.

subfiles.title: Certification of FEC decision
subfiles.about: A copy of the FEC decision is certified against the original.
subfiles.summary: Certifies the attached decision as a true copy.

subfiles.title: Interim reparations removals: Synthetic oil and synthetic rubber industries
subfiles.about: The FEC specifies which synthetic oil and rubber facilities should be available for claim.
subfiles.summary: All facilities qualify, except synthetic oil plants needed for fertilizer production until other fixed nitrogen supplies suffice.

subfiles.title: Draft directive on synthetic industries
subfiles.about: State proposes transmitting the FEC synthetic industries decision to SCAP as a directive.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum asks for JCS transmission and secure handling before press release. The attached draft quotes the FEC policy on synthetic oil, synthetic rubber, and a fertilizer plant exception.

subfiles.title: Change in reparations selections within Japanese industry
subfiles.about: A SCAP revision substitutes the Osaki bearing factory for Nihon Seiko’s Tamagawa factory.
subfiles.summary: Reports the substitution and encloses SCAPIN 1184.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1184: Revision of SCAPIN 1136
subfiles.about: SCAP replaces one Nihon Seiko factory on the precision bearing reparations list.
subfiles.summary: Deletes Tamagawa and adds Osaki, with Japanese representatives to receive implementation instructions.

subfiles.title: Proposed Indian industrial study visit
subfiles.from: John H. Hilldring, for the Acting Secretary of State
subfiles.about: State declines an Indian request to send a group to study Japanese industrial techniques.
subfiles.summary: Because economic conditions and facilities in Japan remain unsettled, State cannot arrange the visit. It promises to reconsider when conditions permit.

subfiles.title: Reply to SCAP on assured minimum industrial levels
subfiles.about: A draft cable outlines FEC negotiations over Japan’s assured industrial capacity.
subfiles.summary: It describes British, Chinese, and Soviet positions and seeks authority to compromise on capacity figures and advance agreed items separately.

subfiles.title: Revised reply to SCAP cable C 64806
subfiles.about: A fuller draft response replaces an earlier message on assured industrial levels.
subfiles.summary: Requests consideration of a revised cable and destruction of the earlier draft.

subfiles.title: Cable to SCAP regarding minimum industrial level program
subfiles.about: Approval is requested for a cable addressing SCAP’s call for quick FEC action.
subfiles.summary: Says the U.S. FEC member is pressing priority consideration of assured industrial levels.

subfiles.title: Status of assured capacity paper
subfiles.about: A proposed cable explains FEC delay and possible compromises on capacity figures.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes British positions and possible Chinese and Soviet objections; proposes negotiating lower figures and adopting agreed items promptly.

subfiles.title: Assured production capacity levels for Japan
subfiles.about: Whitman seeks authority to accept reasonable reductions in U.S. proposed retention levels.
subfiles.summary: He prioritizes FEC agreement on assured retention and requests discretion before the 17 September committee meeting.

subfiles.title: SCAP cable C 64806
subfiles.about: SCAP urges early FEC approval of assured minimum industrial levels.
subfiles.summary: SCAP warns that reparations, financial measures, and zaibatsu dissolution make Japanese industry precarious.

subfiles.title: Record of telephone authorization to Whitman
subfiles.about: The memorandum records Clayton’s authorization to accept reasonable changes in retention levels.
subfiles.summary: Confirms Whitman’s authority to negotiate changes for the reasons in his earlier memorandum.

subfiles.title: Urgent approval note on Whitman authorization
subfiles.about: A brief handwritten exchange approves advising Whitman.
subfiles.summary: Records agreement to notify Whitman.

subfiles.title: State concurrence on reparations cable
subfiles.about: Claxton confirms State concurrence and a wording change to a cable.
subfiles.summary: Confirms that SWNCC will prepare instructions for the U.S. reparations delegate.

subfiles.title: Reparations and level of industry in Japan
subfiles.about: Claxton seeks approval of a cable explaining U.S. plans for industrial capacity decisions.
subfiles.summary: The proposed cable assigns broad principles to the FEC and industry decisions to a Reparations Conference, seeks SCAP’s views, and proposes a SCAP observer.

subfiles.title: Proposed cable to SCAP on reparations and industry
subfiles.about: The draft conveys the U.S. approach to industrial levels and requests SCAP’s detailed recommendations.
subfiles.summary: It places industry decisions with a proposed Reparations Conference and asks whether SCAP supports sending an observer.

subfiles.title: Draft cover memorandum to Colonel Chard
subfiles.about: Claxton asks that a draft cable identify the JCS determination clearly.
subfiles.summary: Requests clearer attribution of the decision conveyed to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Revised draft cable to SCAP
subfiles.about: The cable draft explains the division of industrial capacity decisions between the FEC and Reparations Conference.
subfiles.summary: It requests SCAP comments and asks about a conference observer.

subfiles.title: Cover memorandum to Colonel Chard
subfiles.about: Claxton requests explicit attribution of the proposed cable’s policy to the JCS.
subfiles.summary: Seeks a call about clarifying the JCS determination in the draft.

subfiles.title: Martin memorandum on SCAP’s industrial capacity proposal
subfiles.about: Martin explains why SCAP’s views are needed despite rejection of its proposed FEC procedure.
subfiles.summary: He recommends asking SCAP for detailed capacity views and its opinion on representation at the Reparations Conference.

subfiles.title: Duplicate cover memorandum to Colonel Chard
subfiles.about: Another copy asks that JCS responsibility be clear in the proposed SCAP cable.
subfiles.summary: Repeats Claxton’s request to clarify the source of the determination.

subfiles.title: Draft cable on industrial levels
subfiles.about: The draft seeks SCAP’s detailed views and asks about a reparations observer.
subfiles.summary: Sets out the U.S. position on FEC principles and later industry decisions.

subfiles.title: Martin memorandum and draft radio to SCAP
subfiles.about: Martin proposes obtaining SCAP’s detailed recommendations and conference observer views.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum explains the JCS response to SCAP’s proposal. Its draft radio assigns broad principles to the FEC and detailed industry decisions to the Reparations Conference.

subfiles.title: Duplicate radio draft to SCAP
subfiles.about: A further copy asks for SCAP’s industrial capacity comments and opinion on an observer.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the proposed division of FEC and conference responsibilities.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Claxton memorandum
subfiles.about: Claxton again seeks clarity about JCS attribution in the SCAP cable.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the cover request for a wording change.

subfiles.title: Additional draft cable to SCAP
subfiles.about: Another cable draft describes proposed reparations procedures and requests SCAP input.
subfiles.summary: Asks for detailed comments and an opinion on observer participation.

subfiles.title: SCAP cable C 64821
subfiles.about: SCAP acknowledges the pending request on reparations and industrial levels.
subfiles.summary: Promises a reply at the earliest opportunity.

subfiles.title: WAR 99017 to SCAP
subfiles.about: Washington sends its position on industrial capacity decisions and seeks SCAP’s advice.
subfiles.summary: The FEC will decide broad principles; a Reparations Conference will address industries. SCAP is asked for recommendations and approval of an observer.

subfiles.title: SCAP cable C 64436
subfiles.about: SCAP gives a timetable for comments on Japan reparations.
subfiles.summary: Comments are being prepared for delivery before 15 September.

subfiles.title: SCAP cable C 62237 on reducing Japanese industrial war potential
subfiles.about: SCAP comments paragraph by paragraph on proposed reductions in Japanese industrial war potential.
subfiles.summary: SCAP generally concurs but proposes flexibility on merchant ship size, authority to dissolve war facility operators, and FEC capacity decisions on SCAP recommendation. It warns that plant claims could damage Japan’s recovery and seeks changes to recordkeeping and controls.

subfiles.title: Authorization to mention an interim directive
subfiles.about: Whitman is authorized to threaten an interim U.S. directive if the FEC stalls.
subfiles.summary: Confirms conditional authority to use the threat during committee negotiations.

subfiles.title: Whitman request for interim directive authority
subfiles.about: Whitman proposes a possible interim directive to speed FEC action on industrial levels.
subfiles.summary: He suggests levels near 75 percent of U.S. figures, with a possible lower sulphuric acid figure, and seeks authority to raise the threat conditionally.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Directive Serial No. 59
subfiles.about: SWNCC forwards copies of the directive on synthetic industries.
subfiles.summary: Allocates one copy for the FEC and two for State files.

subfiles.title: Directive Serial No. 59: Synthetic oil and synthetic rubber
subfiles.about: The FEC policy on synthetic oil and rubber removals is transmitted for SCAP’s guidance.
subfiles.summary: Synthetic oil and rubber plants are made available for reparations claims. Oil plants suited to ammonia fertilizer production remain operating until other fixed nitrogen supplies are adequate.

subfiles.title: Filing Directive Serial No. 59 with the FEC
subfiles.about: State submits a certified copy of the directive for FEC files.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the certified directive under the FEC terms of reference.

subfiles.title: Approval of U.S. policy on steel rolling removals
subfiles.about: SWNCC reports approval of its steel rolling capacity paper and bars public release.
subfiles.summary: Forwards approved copies for State and the U.S. FEC representative.

subfiles.title: Decision amending SWNCC 236/22
subfiles.about: The Secretariat announces approval and a replacement page for the steel rolling paper.
subfiles.summary: Instructs holders to substitute revised page 247.

subfiles.title: SWNCC 236/22 circulation note
subfiles.about: The steel rolling proposal is circulated for committee consideration and JCS comment.
subfiles.summary: Introduces the State member’s memorandum and enclosure.

subfiles.title: Request for determination of steel rolling policy
subfiles.about: State urges an early interim steel rolling decision in response to Chinese interest.
subfiles.summary: Argues that removing iron and steel capacity without rolling equipment would be of limited use to China and asks SWNCC to consider the attached proposal.

subfiles.title: Interim removals: Steel rolling capacity
subfiles.about: A policy study proposes the level of steel rolling capacity Japan should retain during interim reparations.
subfiles.summary: The proposal makes capacity above that needed for three million metric tons of annual rolled steel output available for reparations. Appendices compare U.S., SCAP, Chinese, British, and Pauley figures and discuss primary and secondary mills, including Yawata, Hirohata, Kawasaki, Wanishi, and Kamaishi. The analysis relates rolling capacity to steel ingot output and Japan’s projected peacetime needs.

subfiles.title: Transmission of approved steel rolling policy
subfiles.about: State sends the approved steel rolling policy and requests confidentiality.
subfiles.summary: Forwards SWNCC 236/22 and asks that none of it be publicly released.

subfiles.title: Copy of SWNCC steel rolling cover memorandum
subfiles.about: A second copy reports approval of the steel rolling policy.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the transmission and public release restriction.

subfiles.title: British policy on Japanese industries
subfiles.about: The embassy forwards a parliamentary statement and press clippings on British policy toward Japanese industry.
subfiles.summary: Cripps argues that security reductions in Japanese heavy industry must still leave Japan able to earn its way through lighter industries and exports. Britain seeks fair labor and trade conditions but does not propose a specific Japanese wage standard. The despatch encloses the Commons record and Manchester Guardian clippings.

subfiles.title: Parliamentary Debates: Japanese Industries (Future)
subfiles.from: Stafford Cripps and members of the House of Commons
subfiles.about: Cripps begins a statement on Britain’s approach to Japan’s postwar industries and trade.
subfiles.summary: The extract includes questions on other trade matters before Cripps addresses Japanese industry. He outlines Allied plans to cut industries with war potential, take surplus assets as reparations, and preserve enough export capacity for Japan to become internationally solvent. The statement continues beyond page 395.
